package_info.why_malicious: The package was backdoored at the vendor level, introducing a malicious DLL (nssock2.dll) that enabled remote access and control by attackers. This allowed adversaries to compromise any organization that installed the affected update, providing a covert foothold and data exfiltration capabilities.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the DLL is loaded by the application)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: ShadowPad backdoor code (Win32.Trojan.Shadowpad) embedded in nssock2.dll, as detected by AV engines and behavioral analysis.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes a covert communication channel to a remote command and control server, receives and executes attacker commands, and can exfiltrate sensitive data from the host system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The DLL contains code that is not present in the legitimate version, enabling remote command execution and data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate network library DLL should not initiate outbound connections to unknown servers or execute arbitrary remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools may have similar capabilities, but only with explicit user consent and proper authentication.
key_indicators: Presence of network beaconing and C2 communication code
Ability to execute arbitrary commands from remote server
Detected as Win32.Trojan.Shadowpad by multiple AV engines
Code not present in previous known-good version

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the Android app is installed and permissions are granted)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Android.Trojan.Exod code requesting camera, location, microphone, networking, and SMS read permissions.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accesses the device camera, microphone, and location services, reads SMS messages, and transmits collected data to a remote server over the network.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The app requests a broad set of sensitive permissions not justified by its stated functionality, and combines data collection with network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should only request permissions necessary for their core function, and should not silently exfiltrate sensitive user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Parental control or enterprise monitoring apps may request similar permissions, but with user awareness and consent.
key_indicators: Unjustified access to camera, microphone, and location
Detected as Android.Trojan.Exod by AV engines

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the software vendor's build or update process and injects a malicious DLL (ShadowPad) into the distributed package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious DLL is distributed to and installed by downstream organizations.

attack_chain.action: Victim organization installs the compromised software update, loading the malicious DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes on victim systems.

attack_chain.action: Malicious DLL establishes a covert channel to the attacker's C2 server, enabling remote command execution and data exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent access and can steal sensitive data.

attack_chain.action: In the case of mobile supply chain attacks (e.g., Exodus), the malicious app is distributed via a trusted app store, installed by users, and abuses permissions to exfiltrate data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user data from infected devices.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from DLLs or app components
Execution of arbitrary commands received from remote servers
Access to sensitive device features (camera, microphone, location) without clear justification
Combination of data collection and network exfiltration in non-security apps
file_indicators: Presence of nssock2.dll with hash f1a181d29b38dfe60d8ea487e8ed0ef30f064763
Android APKs requesting camera, microphone, location, and SMS read permissions together
Unexpected changes in capabilities/indicators between software versions
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known ShadowPad C2 infrastructure
Android apps connecting to suspicious remote servers for data exfiltration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor for unexpected network activity from software components, compare new software versions against known-good baselines for added capabilities or indicators, and flag apps or packages that request excessive permissions or exhibit suspicious combinations of data access and network communication. Use automated tools (e.g., ReversingLabs A1000) to scan and compare software updates before deployment.
